entries.claim: The pinned Latin Mass data independently corroborate the component's substantive Latin except the participle deprecántes, which they omit (an omission ruled against the printed page at w047), and expose accidental editorial variants for collation.

locator.section: Postcommunio continuing Monday after the first Sunday of the Passion, above the Tuesday heading; Per Dominum nostrum through Deus.

entries.claim: This separate Postcommunion prints the accented conclusion with no comma after Christum and the colon and uppercase Qui after tuum, ending with Deus. The composite uses nostrum through Deus.; the cue words Per eúndem Dóminum come from p. 40, and this page supplies neither the final duration nor Amen.

locator.section: Top conclusion and response before the Nativity preface dialogue; Per omnia saecula saeculorum. R. Amen.

entries.claim: The top chant line prints Per omnia saecula saeculorum and the response Amen. The composite joins musical syllable divisions and omits the response marker. Only these five words are used; the Nativity preface dialogue and body are excluded.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 115 a; Father-addressed oration conclusion

entries.claim: RG 115 a supplies the full Father-addressed conclusion, ending with Amen. It controls the expansion rule, not the selected composite transcript's accents or its accidental seams.

locator.section: Rubricae generales 116; other particular conclusions noted in the liturgical books

entries.claim: RG 116 keeps the particular conclusions the liturgical books note. Page 40 prints Per eúndem Dóminum. for this Secret, which does not name the Son in its opening clause (its later clause names Him only through His Mother, Deíparæ Vírginis), so RG 115 b does not prescribe it; the printed cue controls, and RG 115 a supplies the formula it abbreviates.

locator.section: RG 480–481, 511 d/i, 513–514; Ordo Missae rubric and chant formula after the secrets

entries.claim: The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.

locator.section: Proper body and abbreviated conclusion cue; full ending supplied from the printed formulae on pp. 123 and 226 under RG 115 a and RG 116

entries.claim: This proper-page locus supplies the body and the abbreviated conclusion cue, not the expanded ending.
